statci

Automated statistical CI/CD for R: 20-rule AST methodological linter with incremental Git-diff PR linting & SARIF 2.1.0 export, Simulation-Based Calibration (SBC) & power-curve fuzzing, parallel RNG invariance testing, Quarto/RMarkdown/LaTeX manuscript auditing, adversarial sensitivity, and multiverse specification-curve robustness suites.

Documentation: https://marcusharrisphd.com/statci/

Why statci?

Software teams rely on static analyzers, fuzzers, and continuous integration to catch subtle defects before release. Quantitative pipelines and academic manuscripts routinely suffer from silent statistical bugs that standard R tooling misses:

  • lintr checks formatting and style—not unseeded stochastic calls, parallel RNG collisions, duplicate worker seeds, train/test data leakage, uncentered multilevel interactions, unvalidated stepwise selection, or silent listwise mismatches.
  • statcheck only checks internal APA p-value arithmetic—it cannot inspect R code, cross-check prose and tables against saved R model objects, or audit estimators via simulation.
  • testthat validates deterministic code logic—not probabilistic properties like Type-I error calibration, exact Clopper-Pearson interval coverage, power monotonicity, rank uniformity, or robustness under data perturbations.

statci unifies five verification pillars into a single CRAN-ready workflow with .statci.yml project orchestration, SARIF 2.1.0 GitHub Code Scanning, standalone HTML/Markdown audit reports, and a security-hardened GitHub Actions generator.

Installation 

# Install development version from GitHub
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("MarcusHarrisUConn/statci")

Five Verification Pillars

1. AST-Based Statistical Linter & Incremental PR Diff Linting (stat_lint(), stat_lint_dir(), stat_lint_diff(), export_statci_sarif())

Parses .R, .qmd, and .Rmd files into full XML abstract syntax trees (preserving exact original line numbers and cross-chunk scope in Quarto/RMarkdown documents) and evaluates 20 built-in methodological rules plus user-registered custom rules (new_stat_rule(), register_stat_rule()):

Rule ID Severity Hazard Detected
unseeded_randomness error Top-level stochastic calls (rnorm, sample, boot, kmeans, etc.) without prior set.seed() / withr::with_seed()
unsafe_parallel_rng error mclapply / parLapply / foreach %dopar% / future_* without L’Ecuyer-CMRG, clusterSetRNGStream(), doRNG, or future.seed
duplicate_parallel_seed error Constant set.seed(42) inside loops or parallel workers generating identical duplicate replications
preprocessing_before_split error scale(), prcomp(), preProcess(), or imputation applied to the full dataset before train/test splitting
in_sample_prediction_eval warning Evaluating RMSE, MAE, AUC, or MSE on training-set predictions rather than held-out test/CV data
uncentered_mlm_interaction warning Fixed-effect interactions in lmer/glmer/lme/glmmTMB/brm using raw uncentered predictors
silent_listwise_mismatch warning Comparing models with differing variable sets via anova()/AIC()/BIC() on unharmonized data
silent_factor_drop warning as.numeric(factor_var) level-code coercion or modeling subset()/filter() data without droplevels()
silent_na_coercion warning Unchecked as.numeric()/as.integer() coercion of character/parsed strings without anyNA()/is.na() verification
unverified_merge_cardinality warning dplyr::*_join() or merge() without relationship = or nrow() guards against silent many-to-many row duplication
missing_drop_false_matrix warning 2D matrix/array subsetting (X[, cols], X[idx, ]) missing drop = FALSE, silently collapsing 1-row/1-col subsets to vectors
implicit_na_rm_masking info Unconditional na.rm = TRUE in summary statistics without nearby missingness inspection (is.na(), anyNA(), complete.cases())
equality_on_float warning Exact == / != comparisons on floating-point literals or continuous statistics
unadjusted_multiple_testing warning Repeated hypothesis tests inside loops/lapply/map without p.adjust() in scope
stepwise_selection_unvalidated warning In-sample step() / MASS::stepAIC() / regsubsets() without cross-validation or holdout validation
missing_convergence_check warning lmer/glmer/optim/nlminb fits without programmatic AST checks for isSingular() or $convergence
global_seed_override_in_fn warning Bare set.seed() inside reusable functions or \(x) lambdas without restoring .Random.seed
short_logical_literal warning Mutable T/F symbols instead of TRUE/FALSE
cor_without_use_arg info cor()/cov() called without explicit use = missing-data handling
absolute_path_in_script warning Hardcoded non-portable paths (/Users/..., C:\..., ~/...) breaking CI 
library(statci)

# Lint a script, Quarto document, or project directory
res <- stat_lint(system.file("examples", "flawed-analysis.R", package = "statci"))
res

# Incrementally lint only added/modified lines in a Git PR without legacy noise
pr_res <- stat_lint_diff(path = ".", base_ref = "origin/main", head_ref = "HEAD")

# Export SARIF 2.1.0 JSON for GitHub Code Scanning inline PR annotations
sarif <- export_statci_sarif(res)

2. Estimator Calibration, SBC, Power Curves & Parallel RNG (audit_estimator(), audit_sbc(), audit_power_curve(), check_parallel_rng())

Verifies custom or standard estimators using Monte Carlo SE-aware decision rules and exact Clopper-Pearson binomial intervals:

est_audit <- audit_estimator(
  dgp = function() {
    x <- rnorm(100)
    z <- rnorm(100)
    data.frame(x = x, z = z, y = 1 + 0.8 * x + rnorm(100))
  },
  estimator = function(df) lm(y ~ x + z, data = df),
  true_params = c(x = 0.8, z = 0.0),
  n_sim = 150L,
  check_parallel = TRUE,
  seed = 42L
)

pc_audit <- audit_power_curve(
  dgp = function(d) rnorm(40, mean = d, sd = 1),
  test_fn = function(y) t.test(y, mu = 0),
  effect_grid = c(0, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75),
  n_sim = 100L,
  target_effect = 0.50,
  target_power = 0.80
)

3. Manuscript-to-Code Consistency Auditor (audit_manuscript())

Cross-checks prose statistics and tables (b, SE, 95% CI, p, N, t, F, chi2, r, R^2, OR, AIC) in .qmd, .Rmd, and .tex manuscripts against saved R model objects (lm, glm, lmerMod, htest, or tidy tables)—plus interval-arithmetic internal consistency checks (t vs b / SE, 95% CI symmetry and width):

fit <- lm(mpg ~ wt, data = mtcars)
audit_manuscript(
  system.file("examples", "sample-manuscript.qmd", package = "statci"),
  models = list(primary = fit)
)

4. Adversarial Sensitivity & Multiverse Specification Curves (audit_sensitivity(), audit_multiverse())

Stress-tests fitted pipelines across tail winsorization, leave-one-cluster-out (LOCO) / leave-one-out jackknife influence, missingness + imputation contrasts, cluster/observation bootstrap stability, and full Cartesian multiverse specification curves with per-fork variance decomposition (eta_squared) and two-panel plot() visualizations:

sens <- audit_sensitivity(
  data = mtcars,
  fit_fn = function(d) lm(mpg ~ wt + hp, data = d),
  n_boot = 100L,
  seed = 42L
)

mv <- audit_multiverse(
  data = mtcars,
  decisions = list(
    outliers = c("none", "winsor_5pct"),
    covariates = c("bivariate", "adjusted")
  ),
  fit_fn = function(d, spec) {
    if (spec$outliers == "winsor_5pct") {
      qs <- quantile(d$mpg, c(0.05, 0.95))
      d$mpg <- pmin(pmax(d$mpg, qs[1]), qs[2])
    }
    if (spec$covariates == "bivariate") lm(mpg ~ wt, data = d) else lm(mpg ~ wt + hp, data = d)
  },
  param = "wt"
)
plot(mv)

5. Declarative Config, Unified Reports & GitHub Actions (read_statci_config(), statci_audit_project(), use_statci_github_action()) 

# Run full project audit driven by .statci.yml
rep <- statci_audit_project(".", enforce_gate = TRUE)

# Generate hardened .github/workflows/statci.yaml with optional SARIF upload
use_statci_github_action(lint_paths = c("R", "analysis"), upload_sarif = TRUE)
